articles.title: SBS 2026: Weaving a Decade of Youth Action for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
articles.summary: 2030 YFPH marks 10 years of youth leadership and sustainable action at SDG Bayanihan Summit 2026!
articles.byline: 2030 Youth Force of the Philippines, Inc. (YFPH)

blocks.text: 2030 Youth Force of the Philippines, Inc. (YFPH) is set to gather young leaders, advocates, organizations, partners, and stakeholders for the upcoming SDG Bayanihan Summit 2026 (SBS 2026) as part of the organization’s 10th year anniversary of youth leadership and sustainable action happening on 23-25 October in Biñan, Laguna.

Carrying this year’s theme “BIGKIS: Binding a Decade of Action, Onward to 2030”, the three-day summit event will serve as an avenue for young Filipinos to strengthen partnerships, mobilize connections, exchange meaningful discussions, and transform their initiatives into tangible actions aligned with the 17 Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations.

The term “Bigkis” is a Filipino word which means to make a bond, tie, or connect pieces of collective actions. Facing a decade of youth action, the summit will underscores the importance of unity and collaboration in addressing critical challenges and pressing issues faced by the underprivileged and marginalized sectors of the country.

The SDG Bayanihan Summit 2026 will provide opportunities for the participants to engage in roundtable discussions and masterclasses, immerse in plenary sessions and interactive booths, and formulate concrete ways on translating youth-led advocacies into effective programs and strategies.

More than a summit, the SBS 2026 in its tenth year of giving significant voices and spaces, is an eye-opener for the Filipinos to reinforce and ignite passion in volunteerism and bayanihan. While several SDGs are showing regression, the call for intensive youth participation is an imperative to achieve the Philippine’s pursuit of the 2030 agenda and targets, highlighting the necessity for stronger innovative solutions and sustainable actions.
When people are united by a common purpose, the spirit of bayanihan and volunteerism becomes a powerful catalyst for change and action.
Take part in the biggest bayanihan for the global goals! Register now via bit.ly/sbsregular, fee starts at P3000.00.
Follow SDG Bayanihan Summit and 2030 Youth Force of the Philippines on Facebook for updates.

articles.title: Leonen: We need to think if bar exam should be the 'be all, end all'
articles.summary: Supreme Court (SC) Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen, a candidate for the position of chief justice, said Thursday that there is a need to review whether the Bar Examinations for aspiring…

blocks.text: Published October 22, 2026 2:50pm

Supreme Court (SC) Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen, a candidate for the position of chief justice, said Thursday that there is a need to review whether the Bar Examinations for aspiring lawyers should be the primary mode of who is qualified to practice law in the country.
"The cultural pressure that we put on the Bar Exam is too tremendous," he said.

"I think we need to rethink whether it should be the be all and end all of any law school. And I think our law school curriculum should follow whatever the admission process is," said Leonen, a former professor at the University of the Philippines (UP) College of Law.
Leonen made the remark during his interview by the Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) for position of chief justice, which will be vacated by incumbent Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo.

"My question always is, for an architect to become an architect, why is it that they need to practice first architecture under the supervision of an architect for thousands of hours before they take the board exam?" he said.
"By the time they take the board exam, they are now so familiar with what is required in architecture that it is already easy," he added.
During his interview for position of chief justice, Leonen said the method of teaching in classrooms should be changed.
He said sometimes, the Socratic method does not create critical minds.

"Sometimes the Socratic method does not really work. The Socratic method is really incantating the student to be subservient to a doctrine and not creating more critical minds. So that is one concept that I think we need to review," he said.

Leonen was interviewed by Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, Senator Kiko Pangilinan, Batangas Representative Gerville Luistro, retired SC Associate Justice Jose Catral Mendoza, lawyer Nesauro Firme, retired Court of Tax Appeals Associate Justice Erlinda Piñera, and lawyer Jose Meija.

articles.title: Bangko Sentral raises interest rates to 5.50% as inflation, peso woes mount
articles.summary: Even as the central bank tries to keep inflation in check, higher interest rates can only do so much

blocks.text: Facade of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
Even as the central bank tries to keep inflation in check, higher interest rates can only do so much

items: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas raised its benchmark interest rate by 50 basis points to 5.50% due to rising inflation and a weakening peso.
Inflation jumped to 7.2% in September, significantly above the BSP's target, with core inflation reaching a three-year high of 4.7%.
The BSP aims to curb spending and inflation through higher borrowing costs, but challenges remain due to supply-side pressures and a slowing economy.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) raised its benchmark interest rate by 50 basis points to 5.50% as inflation fears and a weakening peso piled on pressure for the central bank to keep borrowing costs high.
BSP Governor Eli Remolona Jr. announced the Monetary Board’s decision on Thursday, October 22, marking the fourth consecutive increase in the target reverse repurchase rate this year.

The decision follows a jump in inflation to 7.2% in September from 6.1% in August, well above the BSP’s 2% to 4% target. Core inflation, which excludes selected volatile food and energy items, also climbed to the highest point in three years at 4.7%, suggesting that price pressures are spreading across the economy.
Before Thursday’s decision, the BSP had projected inflation to average 6.1% in 2026 and 5.4% in 2027, both above its target range.

blocks.caption: [READOUT] What a stickier inflation wave could mean for businesses

blocks.text: The weakening peso has further aggravated concerns. The currency closed at a record-low P63.361 against the dollar on Wednesday, October 20. A weaker peso makes imported fuel, food, and raw materials more expensive, adding to domestic inflation.

By making borrowing more expensive, the BSP hopes to slow spending and ease inflation. But higher interest rates could also weigh on consumption and investment at a time when Philippine economic growth has already slowed to just 2.3% in the second quarter.

There are also limits to what higher interest rates can achieve. Much of the current inflation is driven by supply-side pressures, including disruptions to food production due to bad weather, rising global oil prices, and the threat of El Niño, none of which monetary policy can directly address.
The latest increase was widely expected, with some arguing for even more aggressive tightening.

In an October 20 GlobalSource Partners report, former BSP deputy governor Diwa Guinigundo and economist Wilhelmina Manalac called for a 50-basis-point hike to prevent inflation from becoming more entrenched, while acknowledging the risks to an already struggling economy.

Meanwhile, BPI lead economist Emilio Neri Jr. expects another 25-basis-point increase in December, potentially bringing the policy rate to 5.75% only by year-end. Further hikes in 2027 remain possible, depending on inflation and El Niño.
The Monetary Board’s final scheduled policy meeting for 2026 is on December 17. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Meta ordered to pay $25-billion penalty to New Mexico in data privacy case
articles.summary: 'Facebook's wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the heart of Facebook's core business practices,' Judge Francis Mathew writes in his order

blocks.text: META. The logo of Meta at the Meta Lab in Los Angeles, California, USA, May 20, 2026.
Daniel Cole/Reuters
'Facebook's wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the heart of Facebook's core business practices,' Judge Francis Mathew writes in his order

items: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta Platforms to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company misled consumers about data privacy, stemming from the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
The ruling was described as one of the largest financial penalties against a corporation in US history, with New Mexico's Attorney General emphasizing the need to hold Big Tech accountable.
Meta plans to appeal the decision, arguing that the penalties are excessive and that the state did not prove consumers were misled.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

A judge in New Mexico ordered Meta Platforms on Wednesday, October 21, to pay the state $25 billion after a jury found the company had misled consumers about the privacy of their data, hitting the company with one of the largest financial penalties in US history.

The ruling came in a case stemming from allegations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent. New Mexico had sued Meta, accusing it of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data.

“Facebook’s wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the heart of Facebook’s core business practices,” Judge Francis Mathew wrote in his order, which came more than three weeks after the verdict.
Mathew found that a penalty of more than $219 billion was warranted based on state law, but he reduced the figure to $25 billion.
In a statement, CJ Mahoney, Meta’s chief legal officer, said the company is confident it will win on appeal.

“This ruling, and the Attorney General’s approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico,” Mahoney said. “At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online.”
New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said in a statement after the ruling the penalty was one of the largest financial penalties against a corporation in US history.
Meta previously faced a $5-billion penalty from the US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 over the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

Six other states settled their lawsuits against Meta related to Cambridge Analytica for $459.2 million as part of a $17.1 billion multistate settlement the company reached in August to resolve states’ claims that the company’s platforms had harmed teen mental health.
New Mexico’s attorney general sued Meta in 2021 following revelations that Cambridge Analytica had harvested personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app.

The state accused Meta of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data and its handling of hate speech and misinformation posted on the platform. It alleged the company knew third parties had broad access to users’ data and tolerated hate speech or other harmful content when it benefited the company’s bottom line.
Cambridge Analytica, now defunct, used the data for voter profiling and targeting.

“It has been a long time coming holding Big Tech accountable,” Torrez told a press conference in Albuquerque after Wednesday’s ruling. “I think today’s judgment is a clear break with that past and a very clear warning to those in this space and beyond that we intend to protect our people and protect our consumers.”
Mathew’s decision comes as Meta faces thousands of lawsuits and pressure from lawmakers over the impact of Instagram and Facebook on teen mental health, with another trial slated to begin next week.

Earlier this year, New Mexico won $942 million in a pair oftrials against Meta over claims it facilitated sexual exploitation of young people on Instagram and Facebook and misled consumers about the platforms’ safety.
Analyst Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson & Co, called the latest New Mexico ruling costly but unlikely to impact the company’s value.
“Meta is worth nearly two trillion dollars, and will likely continue to appeal these cases and drag them out,” Luria said.

Jurors in September had found that the company and its leadership made 26 misleading statements on data privacy, hate speech and other subjects. Multiplying those statements by their potential audience, they said the company had committed more than 43 million violations of New Mexico’s consumer protection laws.
At a hearing on October 1, Randi McGinn, a lawyer for New Mexico, had asked Mathew to award the state between $35 billion and $40 billion.
“This court should speak to Meta in the only language it understands, which is money, and the value of its stock price,” McGinn said.

In court filings, Meta urged Mathew to cap the penalties at $3.45 billion. The evidence showed that Meta does not sell user data and New Mexico did not prove that any consumer had actually been misled, the company said in court filings. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Only 25 attend Murad party oath-taking as rival claims 46-member bloc
articles.summary: The political party of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front is not ready to concede the race for Bangsamoro's top leadership post

blocks.text: MURAD'S MESSAGE. MILF chairman and former BARMM interim chief minister Ahod 'Al Haj Murad' Ebrahim delivers keynotes the oath-taking ceremony of lawmakers-elect on Wednesday, Octoober 21, 2026.
Ferdinandh Cabrera/Rappler
The political party of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front is not ready to concede the race for Bangsamoro's top leadership post

items: Only 25 out of 30 lawmakers-elect from the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) attended the oath-taking ceremony, raising questions about their support ahead of the upcoming parliamentary vote.
The Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) claims to have secured a majority coalition with 46 members, while UBJP is still negotiating to retain influence in the government.
Former chief minister Ahod Ebrahim emphasized the importance of unity and collective responsibility, urging political leaders to prioritize public service over personal ambitions.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

COTABATO CITY, Philippines – The numbers were not on former Bangsamoro interim chief minister Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim’s side on Wednesday, October 21. Only 25 newly elected regional lawmakers showed up for the oath-taking of his United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP).

UBJP’s main rival earlier claimed more than enough signatures behind its bid to control the incoming Parliament of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM). But Murad’s party is not ready to concede the race for Bangsamoro’s top leadership post.

The contest pits Murad, chairman of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), against BARMM interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua, whose Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) claimed to have secured a majority coalition ahead of the October 30 vote to choose the Muslim-majority region’s first elected leader.

blocks.caption: OATH. Twenty-five members of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party take their oath as members of the BARMM Parliament at the Shariff Kabunsuan Cultural Complex in Cotabato City on Wednesday, October 21. Ferdinandh Cabrera/Rappler

blocks.text: The contrast was difficult to ignore at the Shariff Kabunsuan Cultural Complex, where the MILF’s political party held its oath-taking ceremony, especially after 46 newly elected members of parliament reportedly signed the coalition agreement backing Macacua, erstwhile MILF top commander and Murad’s former subordinate in the interim Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA).
Yet the UBJP, which counts at least 30 incoming MPs among its members, said attendance at its oath-taking ceremony was not a definitive measure of its support ahead of the parliamentary vote.

“Anyone can release projections for numbers, and until D-Day arrives for the election of the speaker and the chief minister, everything is still possible,” said UBJP secretary-general and spokesperson Mohajirin Ali.

blocks.caption: Macacua secures 46-member coalition backing ahead of BARMM chief minister vote

blocks.text: Only 25 of 30 lawmakers-elect listed under the UBJP attended the ceremony on Wednesday because of health concerns and other reasons, Ali said.
“It doesn’t mean that if you’re absent here, you’re not part of the party; that would be unfair to them,” Ali told a news conference.

The 80-member Bangsamoro Parliament is scheduled to elect its speaker and chief minister when it convenes by the end of the month. Under the Bangsamoro Organic Law, a candidate for chief minister needs at least 41 votes to secure a simple majority.

The September parliamentary elections produced no clear majority, prompting rival political camps to negotiate alliances to secure control of the regional government. The BFP’s claim of a 46-member bloc gives Macacua a projected majority, while Murad’s UBJP is still seeking to retain its influence in the government.
Ali said UBJP members who took their oaths elsewhere, including in Lanao del Sur and at the Supreme Court, or submitted formal notices explaining health-related absences remained part of the party.

He cautioned against interpreting UBJP members’ attendance at gatherings or coalition discussions hosted by rival groups as a sign of defection, describing such interactions as normal political engagement while parties kept communication lines open.

Asked about possible defections or abstentions in the leadership vote, Ali said party-list and sectoral representatives were bound by party discipline, while district representatives had to consider the interests of their constituencies.
He said political turncoatism is a violation under the Bangsamoro Electoral Code.

Ali also said it was expected that the incoming regional government would take the form of a “coalition of parties” rather than a traditional “rainbow coalition,” as no single party had won an absolute majority, and a stable administration would require cooperation among political forces.
Meanwhile, Murad called for unity, discipline and collective responsibility, warning that personal ambitions and political disagreements should not take precedence over public service.

“Do not allow personal interests to weaken our collective purpose. Do not allow political disagreement to distract us from our responsibilities, and do not allow the pursuit of individual recognition to overshadow the vision that brought us together,” Murad told a crowd on Wednesday.
He said public office should not be used to advance personal or family interests, but should serve communities that have endured deprivation, injustice and uncertainty.

Murad also reminded the crowd that the region’s political transformation was a result of generations of sacrifice and resilience as he paid tribute to “martyrs,” Islamic scholars, civil society groups, women, young people and ordinary citizens who had endured conflict and hardship in the struggle for the Bangsamoro people’s homeland, faith and identity.

“The attainment of political autonomy is not the end of our struggle. It is the beginning of a greater responsibility,” Ebrahim said. “The true challenge today is not just preserving the power granted to us, but turning the gains of the peace process into tangible improvements in everyday lives.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Palawan authorities warn of another China rocket launch
articles.summary: Puerto Princesa City — The Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office of the Palawan provincial government warned the public on Thursday about another Long March 8 rocket the People’s Republic of…

blocks.text: Puerto Princesa City — The Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office of the Palawan provincial government warned the public on Thursday about another Long March 8 rocket the People’s Republic of China is set to launch on Sunday, October 25.
The launch is scheduled between 9:42 a.m. and 10:43 a.m., after which rocket debris is expected to fall inside two predetermined drop zones.

Drop Zone 1 includes areas located about 107 nautical miles from Patag Island in the West Philippine Sea, 122 nautical miles from Bajo de Masinloc (Panatag Shoal), 164 nautical miles from El Nido town, and 167 nautical miles from Busuanga town.

Drop Zone 2, on the other hand, is located about 42 nautical miles from Hadji Muhtamad town in Basilan province, 42 nautical miles from the Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park, 53 nautical miles from Pangutaran Island in Sulu, and 122 nautical miles east of Puerto Princesa City.
DZ 1 areas were identified inside the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone (EEZ), while DZ 2 areas are within the waters inside the Philippine archipelago.
Mariners were advised to avoid the designated drop zone during the rocket launch.
Rocket parts such as boosters and payload fairings are designed to be discarded and fall back yo Earth once the launch enters its final stage, and may endanger vessels within the drop zones.
People have been advised to take caution when encountering suspected debris and report it to authorities for proper disposition and handling./coa

articles.title: Philippines exploring deeper cooperation with Taiwan to protect undersea cables
articles.summary: The Philippines is exploring deeper cooperation with Taiwan on protecting undersea cables and addressing "gray-zone" activity, despite Manila's one-China policy, which recognizes Beijing and not…

blocks.text: Published October 22, 2026 2:18pm

WASHINGTON — The Philippines is exploring deeper cooperation with Taiwan on protecting undersea cables and addressing "gray-zone" activity, despite Manila's one-China policy, which recognizes Beijing and not Taipei, a Philippine diplomat said on Wednesday.

The Philippines and Taiwan have repeatedly complained about Chinese activities designed to pressure the countries without direct confrontation. China claims Taiwan as its own territory and has overlapping claims with both Taiwan and the Philippines in the South China Sea.

Felipe F. Carino III, Manila's deputy chief of mission in Washington, told a seminar this "pragmatic and practical approach" with Taiwan was necessary to protect mutual interests in the Bashi Channel between Taiwan and the Philippines.
Speaking to Washington's Center for a New American Security, Carino linked cable security to South China Sea tensions, but did not mention China by name.
He said security of undersea cables was vital given that they carried nearly all intercontinental data flows "and that 60-67% of cyber incidents happen in our region."

"These are very important features that should be protected, so much so that we are exploring deeper cooperation with our friends in Taiwan," Carino said, adding that the Philippines was doing so "notwithstanding our one China policy."

He said the Philippines and Taiwan were exploring "practical and more pragmatic approaches in cooperation, including knowledge-sharing and capacity building" and added: "We see this cooperation leading towards ... addressing the gray-zone issues in our part of the world."

Asked if this cooperation could include joint patrols or accountability for vessels that disrupt communications, Carino said he did not have details, but said: "I'm sure that this is a constantly evolving cooperation, and some of the things that you mentioned may be actually coming to fruition."

Taipei has stepped up efforts to protect undersea communications links, which are vital to the island's connections to the rest of the world, after several incidents involving cables and China-linked vessels.

This month, the Philippine Coast Guard said it had deployed its largest vessel and an aircraft to challenge a Chinese research ship operating off northern Batanes province near undersea cable corridors.

At the same seminar, Andrea Yang, Taiwan's deputy representative in Washington, referred to the jailing in Taiwan of a Chinese ship captain over damage to an undersea cable. She said Taiwan would put more resources into developing unmanned systems to improve maritime surveillance.
Yang said interference with undersea cables was an issue that should be taken up by the United Nations, which should consider mechanisms to prevent "bad behavior." — Reuters

articles.title: Divide and conquer? Teodoro says China meddling with Philippine politics
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro on Thursday said China is already meddling with Philippine politics as more Filipinos turn against each other.

blocks.text: Published October 22, 2026 2:18pm
Defense Secretary Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro on Thursday said China is already meddling in Philippine politics as more Filipinos turn against each other.

“Pinaratangan na nila ako na personal political motive. Nakikialam na sila sa politika dito, hindi na diplomasya ang pinag-uusapan dito. They are already wading into the internal affairs ng Pilipinas at hindi…palalampasin ito,” Teodoro said in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB.

(They have accused me of a personal political motive. They are meddling with the politics here, it is no longer about diplomacy. They are already wading into the internal affairs of the Philippines and this… should not be allowed to pass.)
Asked if there was an effort to divide and conquer, Teodoro said “definitely”.

“Made-de-escalate ito kung manindigan ang Pilipino laban sa kanila, kasi niloloko na tayo nitong mga ito, very obvious na 'to, at pinaghihiwa-hiwalay na tayo. Ang escalation ay hindi nanggagaling sa atin. Factual lang naman ang sinasabi natin laban sa kanila,” he added.

(This will be de-escalated if Filipinos stand up against them, because we are being fooled by them; it is very obvious that we are being divided. The escalation did not come from us. Everything we say against them is true.)

Jing has been drawing criticism after saying last week that China would win if it used force in the West Philippine Sea, something that he said his country would not do. However, some government officials have defended Jing, including Senator Robin Padilla, who claimed that the envoy was a gentleman.
“Opinyon ni Senator Robin iyon, pero opinyon ng nakararami, hindi eh,” Teodoro said.
(That is Senator Robin’s opinion, but the opinion of many is that he is not.)
Legislators from both chambers of Congress have filed their respective resolutions urging President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. to declare Jing as persona non grata.
Following Jing’s comments, the Chinese Embassy has also targeted several Filipino personalities, even going as far as “banning” the House lawmakers behind the resolution from going to China.
Teodoro said that while Jing’s behavior is unacceptable, there were many things for Marcos to consider before he could decide to expel the envoy.
After all, Jing was only acting on the Chinese government’s orders, he added.

“Okay, palitan mo ‘man 'yan. Kung 'yung papalit, ganun pa rin ang ginagawa…Anong silbi? Kaya kailangan, 'yung solusyon dito, matigil 'yung gawain nila at maipaliwanag sa kanila na may hantungan ang pwede nilang gawin dito. Wala sa tao 'yun,” Teodoro said.

(Okay, replace him. But if the person they replace him with is also doing the same thing… then what is the use? So what is needed, the solution here is to stop what they are doing, and explain to them that they have limitations. This is not with the person.)
The Palace earlier stated that Marcos is not inclined to expel Jing, but maintained that this did not mean that the Philippines was relinquishing its claim on the West Philippine Sea.—AOL, GMA News

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Claire Castro not removed from her post, remains Palace press officer
articles.summary: The Palace press officer was still briefing reporters on the day the video was posted, while its thumbnail falsely suggests a supposed confrontation with First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos

blocks.text: Claim: Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro has been removed from her position as Palace press officer.
Why we fact-checked this: A YouTube video posted on October 4 by “PINAS BALITA TV,” credited to “The General’s Viewpoint,” carries the claim.
Text on its thumbnail reads, “Pinatalsik! Castro sibak sa pwesto!”
(Ousted! Castro removed from her post!)
It also shows First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos appearing to confront Castro, alongside the text, “Sinira mo! Ang pangalan ng asawa ko!”
(You destroyed my husband’s name!)
The video is titled, “Heto na! Pinatalsik na sa pwesto? Ante Kler, wala ng takas, nasampolan na? Mayor Baste, rumesbak na?”
(Here it is! Ousted from her post? Ante Kler has no escape, already made an example of? Mayor Baste fights back?)
As of writing, the video has garnered more than 22,000 views and 1,300 likes.
The facts: Castro has not been removed from her post. No Malacañang statement, PCO memorandum, or credible news report has announced her dismissal or resignation.

On October 4, the same day the video was posted, Castro texted reporters on the prosecution’s decision to drop the bribery allegation against Vice President Sara Duterte in her impeachment trial. Castro said the decision was within the prosecution’s discretion but could “shortchange” Filipinos from learning the full truth.

The video does not provide evidence that Castro was supposedly removed from her post. Its commentary instead focuses on Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte’s appearance and testimony during his sister’s impeachment proceedings and criticizes Castro over her remarks about him.

Castro had said Baste Duterte elevated himself as a mayor during his testimony but appeared to throw his sister under the bus when he said that he was not aware of the Vice President’s connection to GenCorp Industries Inc.
The video’s thumbnail also gives the impression that the First Lady confronted Castro, but the video provides no evidence of such an encounter.

Castro remains: Castro did file a courtesy resignation in July 2025 when then-PCO Secretary Dave Gomez assumed office, a standard procedure accompanying a change in agency leadership. Gomez declined to accept it, and Castro has remained in her post since.
The PCO website shows several recent press briefings held by Castro. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: How Arab parties could hold critical balance of power in Israeli election
articles.summary: Disaffection has often driven down turnout among Arab Israelis, but there is a strong push to get rid of the right-wing governing coalition.

blocks.text: Students in Nazareth are handing out leaflets encouraging Arab Israelis to vote in next week's election
ByYolande Knell
Middle East correspondentReporting fromNazareth

At rush hour in Nazareth, the largest Arab-majority city in Israel, students are handing out leaflets by the roadside urging motorists to vote in next week's closely fought, general election. Polls indicate that Arab parties could be left holding a critical balance of power.

Disaffection has often driven down past turnout among Arab Israelis - who account for about a fifth of the population and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel. But this election, there is a strong push to get rid of the most right-wing governing coalition in the country's history - an alliance between veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties.

"I see it as our duty to bring down this extremist government. They treat us as second-class," says Arkan Badran, 23, who is with the students giving out flyers. "I call on all young men and women to vote for Arab lists, which represent us, because this is our future."

blocks.caption: Image caption, All but one of the leading Jewish parties have ruled out forming a coalition government with Arab parties

blocks.text: All but one of the leading Jewish parties have ruled out forming a coalition government with Arab parties
Most opinion polls indicate that neither Netanyahu and his partners nor the main "Change Bloc", led by centre-right former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has a clear path to a parliamentary majority.

If they are right, after the election anti-Netanyahu parties wanting to form a governing coalition would either have to go back on pledges not to work with the prime minister or make a deal with Arab-majority lists.
A major sticking point is that Eisenkot has so far ruled out forming a government with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values.

Israel's politics and society have been changed by the deadly, unprecedented Hamas-led assault on the country on 7 October 2023, and subsequent war in Gaza. There is increased mistrust of and hostility towards the country's Arab minority.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Salman Mousa accuses ministers of "systematic discrimination and incitement" against Arab Israelis

blocks.text: Salman Mousa accuses ministers of "systematic discrimination and incitement" against Arab Israelis

"After October 7, we were treated as enemies of this country," says Suha Salman Mousa of the Mossawa Centre in Nazareth, which advocates for equal rights for Arab citizens. "There was shrinking space for freedom of speech. There were major arrests, there was also firing of people from their workplaces because they put something on social media or they went out against the war on Gaza."

Salman Mousa accuses ministers of "systematic discrimination and incitement" against Arab Israelis. Civil society groups say they have disproportionately cut budgets for Arab communities. The government says reductions are needed to fund wartime defence and security spending.
There have also been politicised campaigns against Arab physicians working in Israeli hospitals and racially motivated attacks on Arab bus drivers by Jewish Israelis.

Some electioneering has sought to capitalise by deepening social divisions. The far-right Finance Minister, Bezalel Smotrich, has vowed to "Judaise" parts of the northern Galilee and southern Negev regions where most Arabs live, likening this to expanding settlements in the occupied West Bank.

The majority of Arab Israelis are descendants of Palestinians who remained within what became Israel during the war that surrounded the creation of the state in 1948, when hundreds of thousands were forced from or fled their homes. Israel's current government often frames them as a threat to the state's Jewish identity. Recently, the prime minister has claimed that his rivals plan to team up with Arabs and form a "dangerous government".

To make this point, his campaign has put up billboards, including one at a road junction at the main entrance to Nazareth. They suggest a choice between: "Right or Palestine" - with pictures of main opposition figures, including right-wingers, depicted as representing the latter not the former. The Netanyahu campaign has also used AI-generated videos to present his opponents embracing Arab leaders.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Radio Nas anchor Mohammed Magadli says Benjamin Netanyahu is trying to delegitimise Arab parties

blocks.text: Radio Nas anchor Mohammed Magadli says Benjamin Netanyahu is trying to delegitimise Arab parties

At Radio Nas, a popular Arabic-language station in Nazareth, I meet news anchor Mohammed Magadli, who is also an analyst for Israel's Channel 12. His father, Raleb Magadli, served as Israel's first Muslim minister between 2007 and 2009, representing the Labour party.
I ask the younger Magadli what he makes of Change Bloc leaders refusing to join forces with Arab parties.

"In a word its racism. But if we're trying to explain why, it's because of the political interests of Benjamin Netanyahu," he says. "He's trying all the time to pull the legitimacy of the Arab parties - because they're Arab, because they're Palestinian. This is affecting the majority of the Jewish parties in Israel."

Polls this week have suggested that both Eisenkot's bloc and Netanyahu's religious-nationalist bloc could each win around 50 seats of the 120 in Israel's parliament while 13 or 14 seats in total could go to Arab-majority groupings.
These are the Joint Arab List, a coalition of Hadash, Balad and Taal, and the smaller United Arab List, an Islamist party headed by politician Mansour Abbas.

blocks.caption: Image caption, United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas wants Arab parties to reach a "position of influence"

blocks.text: United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas wants Arab parties to reach a "position of influence"

While Abbas's party was originally created as part of the Islamic Movement in Israel - which has socially conservative values - he has become known for joining with Jewish partners. He prioritises solving the problems of Arab Israelis and speaks relatively little of Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
Abbas has had a taste of power. In 2021, he became a minister in a previous, short-lived Israeli government led by Naftali Bennett - now a right-wing member of Eisenkot's bloc.

For this election, he has taken the surprise step of giving the number two position on his slate to a Jewish former police official and centrist member of parliament, Yoav Segalovitz. Abbas believes Eisenkot and others will be more open to an alliance with his party after the election and insists he wants to join the next government.

"We've reached the conclusion that parliamentary representation is not enough to serve Arab society. We decided to take responsibility, to become part of the solution to our problems and to offer hope to both Arabs and Jews," he tells me.
"That's why our approach has been driven by a desire to reach a position of influence, not merely representation."

blocks.caption: Image caption, The Joint List talks of providing an electoral "safety net" to those who could replace Netanyahu's government

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
The Joint List talks of providing an electoral "safety net" to those who could replace Netanyahu's government

Meanwhile, the Joint List - which is made up of secular parties and advocates for equal rights for Arab Israelis, an end to Israeli military occupation of Palestinian territories, and a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict - aims to wield a position of influence within the opposition.
It talks of providing an electoral "safety net" to those who could replace the Netanyahu government, in return for support on important policies.
A main issue in this election for Arab Israelis is rampant gang crime.
In September, a poll by the Israel Democracy Institute think tank found that this was the most important factor for 53.5% of Arab citizens when deciding which party to vote for.

Murders within the community reached a record high of 252 last year – about five times higher than the number of Jewish Israelis who were killed, according to the Abraham Initiatives, a Jewish-Arab organisation that promotes coexistence.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Arab Israelis accuse the government of inaction on the issue of gang crime

blocks.text: Arab Israelis accuse the government of inaction on the issue of gang crime
In Jaffa, a mixed Arab-Jewish neighbourhood which is now joined to Tel Aviv, Ziad Samouni shows me where his son, Hussein, was shot dead by two gunmen on a motorcycle near his home last November.
No arrests have been made in his case. With a low percentage of cases solved, Arab-Israelis accuse the government of inaction.

"It seems they're interested in making sure we reach a situation where the killer is never caught, allowing Arabs in Arab society to keep killing one another," says Samouni, who is now part of a support group, Israeli-Palestinian Bereaved Families for Peace.
The Israeli police told the BBC its investigation into Hussein's murder remained active, adding that it took "every case of violence and crime with the utmost seriousness."
"As a father who's lost a son, of course, I want this bloodshed to end," Samouni tells me. "I wish every Arab citizen who believes there needs to be a change sees that this is a time to go to vote."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Ziad Samouni's son Hussein (2nd L) was shot dead last November but no arrests have been made

blocks.text: Image source, Ziad Samouni
Ziad Samouni's son Hussein (2nd L) was shot dead last November but no arrests have been made
This month, Israel's Supreme Court overruled a decision by the Central Elections Committee to disqualify the United Arab List and the Joint List as well as two of their members.

The committee, which is dominated by the governing coalition, argued that they broke a law banning candidates who deny the existence of Israel as a Jewish state. The parties and their representatives strongly denied it.
With just days to go before voting, back in Nazareth, some motorists display flags for their preferred party on their cars.
The stakes are high in this election: Arab citizens could yet decide who wields power in Israel, and they also see this vote as key to their own future in the country.

articles.title: Boos, heckling greet Brady Tkachuk at 1st NHL game back in Ottawa
articles.summary: A chorus of boos awaited Former Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk as he made his return to the ice at Canadian Tire Centre Wednesday night.

image.caption: Florida Panthers' Brady Tkachuk skates during warmups prior to an NHL hockey game against the Ottawa Senators in Ottawa, on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. (Keito Newman/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Ottawa·New
A chorus of boos awaited Former Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk as he made his return to the ice at Canadian Tire Centre Wednesday night.
Deal with the Florida Panthers in June sent Tkachuk to play in the Sunshine State
A chorus of boos awaited former Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk as he made his return to the ice at Canadian Tire Centre Wednesday night.
It was a packed stadium of vocal Sens fans who did not hold back in letting Tkachuk know how they feel about him.
"He's a traitor, there's not much else to say," said fan Jack Kelso.
"He promised he'd give us the [Stanley Cup], but he left."
Earlier this year, the 27-year-old requested a trade to join the Florida Panthers alongside his older brother and podcast co-host, a move that was unpopular with many fans.
Nearly every time Tkachuk took the ice, or touched the puck, chants, often profane in nature, erupted through the stadium.
"I was expecting it, I just didn't think it would be this much," said fan Lesley Miller.
Senators fans Elissa Robillard, left, and Lesley Miller, right, said there was a big reaction to Brady Tkachuk's return to Ottawa. (Emma Weller/CBC)
A number of attendees also altered their Tkachuk jerseys to showcase their new upset with the player, with some replacing his name with that of the team's new captain Thomas Chabot.
Others chose to throw their jerseys onto the ice.
On an episode of his Wingmen podcast, Tkachuk committed to donating any Sens jerseys tossed on the ice by upset fans to the Boys and Girls Club of Ottawa.
Ottawa Senators fans wore altered jerseys of former Senators player Brady Tkachuk at the game between the Senators and the Florida Panthers in Ottawa. (The Canadian Press/Lisa Wallace)
During the game, a video tribute was made to Tkachuk, who waved to the crowd amid the chants.
Shortly after, he scored the first goal of the night in a power-play goal midway through the first period.
The Sens bounced back, winning the game 5-1.
Tkachuk focuses on fun
After the game, Tkachuk said he has no hard feeling towards anyone and just tried to enjoy the experience.
"It's new, those were my teammates not too long ago," he said.
"It was nice to be in front of this passionate fan base," he added when asked about the fan's reaction to his return.
Travis Green, head coach of the Ottawa Senators, said the game felt "as close to a playoff game as you're gonna get."
"It was very emotional, physical, was a hard fought game and I thought our team was excellent tonight," he said.
Tkachuk spent eight seasons with the Senators after being drafted fourth overall in 2018.
He is set to return to the Canadian Tire Centre on March 18.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Jenna Legge is a reporter with CBC in Ottawa. Before that, she worked as a journalist on Prince Edward Island, with earlier stints in Winnipeg and Toronto. She holds a master's degree in international journalism from City University of London, and also studied journalism, law and political science at Carleton University. She can be reached at jenna.legge@cbc.ca

October 22, 2026
CJP leaders freed after undertaking not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar

blocks.caption: Das and Ranka have been seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over voter-roll irregularitiesImage: Sanchit Khanna/Hindustan Times/IMAGO

blocks.text: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released from Tihar Jail on Wednesday after a Special Executive Magistrate declined a police request to extend their judicial custody by three more days, reports said.

The two leaders at the forefront of the protests calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar following voter-list irregularities, furnished personal bonds and sureties of Rs 50,000 (€470; $530) each.
Their written undertakings promised to maintain peace and not call for protests at Jantar Mantar "till such a time that it is denotified in accordance with law."
The iconic protest site was denotified by Delhi Police earlier in October, months after CJP-led protests culminated in the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Das and Ranka were booked for "trespassing" after entering the Jantar Mantar protest site and raising the Indian flag.
The latest CJP protests have called for Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the deletion of voters' names.

articles.title: Tiu Laurel alleges smear campaign by rice smugglers amid import controversy
articles.summary: 'I’m clearly under attack,' Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. tells a Senate panel during a budget hearing

blocks.text: PROBE. Agriculture Secretary Francis Tiu Laurel attends the Senate hearing on the high prices of food and other basic agricultural commodities, on August 20, 2025.
Angie de Silva/Rappler
'I’m clearly under attack,' Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. tells a Senate panel during a budget hearing

items: Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. claims he is the target of an orchestrated attack by smugglers following reports of illegal rice imports linked to him.
The controversy involves a shipment of over 12,000 metric tons of rice from Vietnam, which Tiu Laurel asserts he attempted to stop by canceling the import permit before it arrived.
Calls for Tiu Laurel's temporary leave of absence have emerged due to concerns about conflicts of interest, as he regulates imports while being linked to the importing company.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Following reports of illegal rice imports involving a company linked to him, Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. can only surmise that he is the target of an orchestrated attack by “the hands of smugglers.”

“I’m clearly under attack,” Tiu Laurel said during the budget hearing Wednesday, October 21. “For what reasons I really don’t know but I can only smell the hands of smugglers na tinira namin dati (that we took on before.)”

The “attacks” were reports about a shipment of more than 12,000 metric tons of rice from Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, aboard the M/V Tay Son 2, and its alleged links to Tiu Laurel. The shipment appeared off Davao on September 14, more than a month after the deadline (before July 31) set in the contract between Aditya Birla Global Trading and Planters Products Incorporated (PPI).

What is the connection to the head of the Department of Agriculture (DA)? The company that imported the rice was PPI. Planters Foundation Incorporated, where Tiu Laurel serves as ex officio chairman, holds a majority of PPI’s outstanding shares.
Tiu Laurel’s said he serves as ex officio chairman because of executive issuances, and that he stopped the shipment (by canceling the import permit) before it arrived.

“Imagine ako na nga ‘yung ex-officio ng PPI, alam ko na PPI ‘yan, alam ko PPI din ‘yung consignee, ako pa rin nagpahinto,” said a visibly frustrated Tiu Laurel during the hearing, where he also had printed screenshots of his messages and instructions regarding the shipment ready.
“So is doing a good thing bad? It is not. I did the right thing.”

He said he even sent a boat from their family operations in General Santos to look for the vessel and take pictures. “Talagang hinanap namin (We really looked for it).” Tiu Laurel, a fishing magnate, comes from the family that owns Frabelle.
Agriculture secretaries have served as the ex officio chairman of the foundation. As Leonardo Montemayor, himself a former DA chief, said, “It can be any secretary.”

Since 1984, when the late former president Ferdinand E. Marcos issued Letter of Instructions (LOI) no. 1428, the minister of agriculture and food held the chairmanship of Planters Foundation Incorporated. Other cabinet members make up the foundation’s board, based on the LOI.
Montemayor, along with other groups, nonetheless are calling for Tiu Laurel’s temporary leave of absence as a show of delicadeza.
“How can it be?” Montemayor told reporters Tuesday, October 21. “You are both the investigated and the one regulating imports, issuing permits, and canceling permits.”
By the end of the budget hearing, presided over by Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan, Tiu Laurel said he was willing to be subjected to an inquiry.

“Kung kami may kasalanan, may kasalanan kami,” Tiu Laurel said. “Kung wala kaming kasalanan, masabi na para matigil na to.” (If we’re at fault, then we’re at fault. If it’s not our fault, then let it be revealed so this ends.)

And then there was a moment of sympathy in the room. Senator Pangilinan recounted his time as presidential assistant for food security during the Aquino administration, when the National Food Authority administrator “was framed by traders.”
“What you’re going through, I went through,” said Pangilinan. “And for what? Because we were going after smugglers and traders who were messing up our rice supply.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Airbnb guests freed from chores involving ‘significant effort’ under new global rules
articles.summary:
Accommodation platform acts after long-standing guest complaints over doing dishes, taking out rubbish and stripping beds

Airbnb hosts will no longer be able to ask guests to strip beds or…

blocks.text: Airbnb hosts will no longer be able to ask guests to strip beds or wash dishes under the accommodation platform’s new rules.
The changes, which apply to Airbnb reservations covered by the platform’s global policy, including bookings in Australia, will come into effect on 20 November and limit chores imposed on guests.
Airbnb had long fielded complaints from guests about having to pay cleaning fees, which can be hundreds of dollars, and still complete a list of chores for their host.
Since April 2025, cleaning fees have not been shown to guests. Instead, hosts have been allowed to choose to factor cleaning costs into the total price of the stay.

In a community policy update posted on its website this week, Airbnb said hosts would “generally” no longer be allowed to ask guests to complete tasks that “require significant effort or time or would typically be performed by a cleaner”.
Examples of such tasks include stripping beds of linen, taking rubbish offsite, and washing and putting away dishes, the company said.
The updated guidelines state that hosts can now set seven standard house rules which must be displayed in full at the time of booking – and can also add other “reasonable” requests.
Examples of house rules include check-in and check-out times, limits on how many guests can stay at the property, smoking restrictions, quiet hours, and whether or not pets are allowed.

Reasonable requests depend on “relevant local considerations”. For example, it may be reasonable to ask guests to limit shower time due to local water restrictions, or to dispose of rubbish in an animal-proof container.
While guests shouldn’t be asked to wash and put away dishes under the new guidelines, hosts can ask them to put used dishes in the sink.
“House rules help guests understand what hosts expect, but we’ve heard from our community that they can be confusing, onerous and hard to manage,” an Airbnb spokesperson said.
“So we’ve redesigned them to make them easier to discover and clearer to set, alongside a new policy that keeps requests reasonable, with no surprises.”

articles.title: Taiwan probes organized crime links to China’s ‘transnational repression’
articles.summary: Taiwan has complained that Beijing is using various underhanded methods to go after Taiwanese who the Chinese government views as separatists or are otherwise politically suspect

blocks.text: TAIWAN SECURITY OFFICIAL. Taiwan National Security Bureau Director-General Tsai Ming-yen speaks to members of the media at the parliament in Taipei, Taiwan, October 22, 2026.
Fabian Hamacher/REUTERS
Taiwan has complained that Beijing is using various underhanded methods to go after Taiwanese who the Chinese government views as separatists or are otherwise politically suspect

items: Taiwan is investigating organized crime's connections to Chinese efforts of transnational repression, particularly following an attack on a comedian who criticized President Xi Jinping.
Taiwan's National Security Bureau is concerned about local criminal networks potentially funded by the Chinese Communist Party, emphasizing the need to dismantle these groups.

Taiwan is facing increased maritime pressure from China, with concerns over Chinese Coast Guard and militia activities near its waters, which Taiwan views as a preparation for potential military actions.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

TAIPEI, Taiwan – Taiwan is probing organized crime’s links to Chinese efforts to carry out “transnational repression,” a security official said on Thursday, October 22, after Taipei’s government said Beijing was behind an attack on a comedian who mocked President Xi Jinping.

Taiwan, which China views as its own territory over the island’s objections, has complained that Beijing is using various underhanded methods to go after Taiwanese who the Chinese government views as separatists or are otherwise politically suspect.

Speaking to reporters at parliament, Taiwan National Security Bureau Director-General Tsai Ming-yen said the local networks that cooperate in incidents like the comedian attack are mostly criminal gangs, or private investigation firms linked to organized crime.

“The National Security Bureau is more concerned with whether anyone behind them has been directed and funded by the Chinese Communist Party. How to dismantle the entire criminal group and network is a key focus for us,” Tsai said.
China’s Taiwan Affairs Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It has not responded to previous questions on the assault on the comedian.
Other China critics in Taiwan have also been attacked, including Hong Kong singer and activist Denise Ho. She was attacked in 2019 in Taipei by a masked man who threw red paint at her.
Tsai said Taiwan might need to amend its laws to better deal with China’s activities.

“Comprehensively curbing the Chinese communists’ transnational repression in Taiwan’s democratic and rule-of-law society is also very important, and the legal framework for it has been lacking,” he added.

Taiwan’s Supreme Prosecutors Office said in a separate statement on Thursday that the public should “raise their vigilance and never assist hostile foreign forces or allow themselves to be exploited as local collaborators.”

Taiwan, whose government rejects Beijing’s sovereignty claims, says it is facing a stepped-up pressure campaign by China, including in the waters around the island where China’s military and Coast Guard operate daily.

Tsai said Chinese Coast Guard activities to the east of Taiwan, where Beijing began what it calls “law enforcement” patrols in June, are becoming more and more routine, often taking place with Chinese research vessels.
He added that he was particularly concerned with the appearance of Chinese militia boats to Taiwan’s east and southwest.
“Generally speaking, militia fishing boats are more commonly seen in the South China Sea, so the emergence of this situation around Taiwan is significant,” Tsai said.

Earlier this month, the US State Department said China’s actions off Taiwan’s east coast are “deeply destabilising” and only worsen tension after Reuters reported the first known sighting of a Chinese militia boat in those waters.
Officials in Taiwan say they believe China is practicing for a possible maritime blockade using overlapping military, paramilitary and civilian assets.
China has repeatedly said its operations off Taiwan’s east coast are “legitimate and lawful” given those are Chinese waters, a position Taipei’s government strongly rejects. – Rappler.com

articles.title: AI firms say UK has a year to head off datacentre protests before construction is threatened
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco taskforce urges ministers to offer areas greater benefits from tech infrastructure amid fears of US-style opposition

AI companies have told ministers…

blocks.text: AI companies have told ministers they have 12 months to head off public opposition to datacentres in the UK or risk US-style protests that could threaten their construction.

Successive dry summers and rising energy bills are increasing public scrutiny of plans for the huge computer warehouses that are used to train and run AI models, says a submission to the Labour government from a group including the AI infrastructure companies Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco.

Amid increasing anti-datacentre activism in the US and Europe, they are calling on ministers to create a “compact” that would show how communities can benefit from hosting datacentres, including allowing councils that host them to retain more tax revenues.

The move by the Sovereign AI Leadership (SAIL) taskforce reflects rising concern among tech companies that arguments that have blocked datacentre developments in parts of the US are taking hold in Britain. Microsoft has promised to invest $30bn (£22bn) in UK AI infrastructure.

Microsoft has built a datacentre in Acton, London and another is under construction in Newport, but wants to build several more facilities and is engaging with local and national leaders, including the prime minister, Andy Burnham, over the balance between the potential benefit of AI to the economy and public opposition to datacentres.

The SAIL group said: “In the United States, organised local opposition has stopped fully permitted datacentre projects, and moratoriums have been announced even in states that are otherwise pro-growth.

“Reporting from those places shows that AI itself is only a surface-level concern; distrust of corporate and government promises, fear of stranded assets and electricity costs run deeper. The same arguments have begun to appear here.”
It added: “Britain has a window – we think of roughly 12 months – to build a compact that earns public consent before that pattern takes hold.”

The taskforce is calling for the government to create a clear framework for councils and mayors to follow that will set out recommended terms for local benefit, including an indicative contribution – likely to be financial or in terms of facilities – scaled to a site’s size.

blocks.caption: The Microsoft Park Royal datacentre in north-west London.  Photograph: Raymond Tang/Alamy

blocks.text: Opposition to datacentre construction is being fuelled by widening public concern about the safety of AI systems, after a summer in which some of the largest companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic and Google appeared to lose control of some of their most cutting-edge AIs. Some protesters have begun resorting to direct action and the membership of anti-AI campaign groups has been growing rapidly.

The datacentre companies are determined to head off that opposition. The chair of the SAIL taskforce, Steve Rigby, said: “By establishing a clear prosperity compact between government, industry and local communities, we can build the infrastructure we need, equip our workforce with future-ready skills, and ensure Britain’s digital destiny. This taskforce’s goal isn’t another strategy document, but high-impact actions that materially accelerate the UK’s transition to an AI-enabled economy.”
It has not calculated the cost to central government finances if councils that grant permission to datacentres are allowed to keep all of their business rates.

Responding to the proposals, Joseph Miller, the director of PauseAI UK, which campaigns for a global pause to datacentre buildout, said: “People are going to feel it is undignified to be bought off by huge tech companies who do not share their interests.”

He said tech companies were “absolutely right to be worried” about US-style public opposition to datacentres growing in the UK. Kat Jones, the director of Action to Protect Rural Scotland, which campaigns against datacentres, said tech companies had already “missed the boat on containing community opposition to hyperscale AI datacentres”.

“In Scotland, we have 15 community campaigns already working incredibly hard opposing these environmentally destructive developments locally, and a growing national campaign,” she said. “Even the titanic lobbying efforts of US big tech are going to find it a real challenge to change the winds of public opinion, which have already shifted solidly against hyperscale AI datacentres.”

Donald Campbell, the director of advocacy at the tech equity campaign Foxglove, said: “Big tech firms have spent years trying to force vast, highly polluting datacentres through the planning system under a blanket of secrecy and misleading information. Now, with the public waking up to the fact that these facilities plunder resources and wreck the climate, the US tech giants have decided that there’s a problem.”

He warned that incentivising councils to back datacentres by allowing them to keep more of their business rate revenue would mean “these wealthy tech giants would not pay a penny more” while boosts to council funding would “come from the pocket of central government services like the NHS”.

A government spokesperson said datacentres “should create British jobs and supply chains, and provide investment to the communities in which they are built, as well as prioritising clean power, using water responsibly”.

“For most proposed datacentre developments, community benefits are considered through the relevant local planning processes,” they said. “We have already announced measures which will enable local authorities hosting datacentres in AI growth zones in England to keep all the additional business rates they generate.”

articles.title: Thursday news quiz: Liz is absurd, Apu finds words and a bloke steals a bird
articles.summary:
Test yourself on topical news trivia, pop culture and general knowledge every Thursday. How will you fare?

The Thursday quiz is aware of standard international units of time, such as the Liz…

blocks.text: The Thursday quiz is aware of standard international units of time, such as the Liz Truss (49 days) and the Scaramucci (11 days). Now a new unit of measurement has entered the chat: the Zacharia (five days). But whatever arbitrary length of time the world invents to measure chaos, political downfalls or social media meltdowns, the Thursday news quiz remains resolutely fixed. It is always seven days apart, unwavering, inescapable and ultimately reliable. Which means, once again, it is time for some questions on topical news, pop culture and general knowledge, with no prizes on offer except pride. Or shame. Allons-y!
The Thursday news quiz, No 270

blocks.caption: Canada

items: 1.Which province of Canada held a referendum this on whether it should have a binding referendum on declaring independence from the country?
2.Archaeologists believe they have solved the mystery of whose bones were buried in a Roman sarcophagus unearthed at Westminster Abbey. Who was it?
3.Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's film about Elizabeth Holmes (pictured) had the biggest documentary debut since 2004 in North America, taking in $15m. What is it called?

4.The Thursday quiz loves trains and saw this lovely steam locomotive in Leicester the other day. But which city in the north of England is to get a brand new station as part of the Northern Powerhouse Rail scheme?
5.Japan (pictured) has launched a space mission to gather rocks from which moon of Mars (also pictured)?
6.A man has been found guilty of animal cruelty after he stole a 27-year-old flamingo from its enclosure at a Las Vegas hotel. What is the bird's name?
7.Send Derren Brown today's collective noun. Use your psychic powers to let him know what, according to Grammar Monster, the collective noun for jaguars is (the animal, not the car).

8.This week's guest canine is Spanner, who the Thursday quiz met in Crouch End. She wants to know the name of the silly bomb-sniffing dog in Utah who accidentally broke several bones when he inexplicably leapt over the side of an overpass while out on a mission?
9.It is Jeff Goldblum's birthday today. Happy birthday, Jeff! Jurassic Park! What's the name of his character in the dinosaur-infused franchise?
10.Apu has his voice back on The Simpsons. Who now voices the character?
11.The Thursday quiz fondly remembers Keith Chegwin, so here is Cheggers plays population! According to the 2026 CIA World Factbook, what is the population of Algeria?
12.England's lady egg chasers (pictured in training) lost their first rugby union match after four years and 41 games unbeaten. Who bested them?
13.A bear in California's Mono county wandered into where to raid the staff snacks and check out the new releases?

14.On this day with Brian May! And his badger! 22 October is the anniversary of a war fought between Britain and Spain from 1739 to 1748, mostly in the Caribbean. The Thursday quiz imagines Queen's legendary guitarist wants you to tell him – and his badger – what it was called.
15.The Thursday quiz regrets to inform you that Liz Truss is at it again, with a new book. What is it called?

16.Bonus question: There is a new Doctor Who story that features a dachshund on the cover, and the writer, Jez Fielder, has posed you this question: In Anton Chekhov’s The Lady with the Little Dog, the lady’s dog is never named. articles.title: Wanted: new No 10 adviser to help citizens deal with rise of AI
articles.summary:
Andy Burnham advertises for policy experts in technology, economic growth and cost-of-living challenges

Andy Burnham is to recruit a number of advisers to plug gaps in No 10, including an…

blocks.text: Andy Burnham is to recruit a number of advisers to plug gaps in No 10, including an expert on how AI will affect society.
The roles advertised by Downing Street give a glimpse into the biggest challenges facing the prime minister – and what he has decided to prioritise.

The new hires will flesh out the threadbare No 10 policy unit – where many of the roles are still vacant after Keir Starmer’s departure. Senior sources have said the prime minister wanted to take time to recruit advisers.

The adviser on AI, who will be expected to have “deep expertise” in the sector, will be expected to lead preparations for the impact of the AI boom on the workforce, amid significant concerns for lower-level professional services jobs, in particular for new graduates.
They will also be expected to be the main adviser to Burnham on frontier AI, the effects and benefits of AI in public service transformation and other major societal impacts.
Several cabinet ministers have openly expressed concerns about the UK’s readiness for the impact of AI on the workforce and economy, as well as the dangers of unregulated systems.

In his Labour conference speech on 28 September, the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, said there were “daunting” dangers of AI, saying they could not allow technological advances “to come at the expense of our children or indeed humanity”.
Burnham will also hire an adviser to develop policy on greater public control over everyday essentials – with a roving brief across transport, energy, housing, water and the environment.
The adviser will be asked to focus on the cost of living. The job advert specifically demands an individual who can “bring challenge and external perspectives into policy development”.
Burnham is known to be frustrated with the cautious and limited options presented to him by Whitehall on areas where he is seeking greater public control.

The Guardian reported on Tuesday that Burnham had told officials to rip up their plans on how to fix Thames Water and present him with more radical choices for what to do with the stricken company, including options that could cost more taxpayer money or carry higher legal risk.

Burnham will also recruit an economic adviser to replace Starmer’s aide, Minouche Shafik. The job, which will examine growth and macroeconomic policy, requires “a strong understanding of the economic, fiscal and political context shaping government decision-making”.

Before he became prime minister, Burnham took advice from Andy Haldane, a former Bank of England chief economist, as well as from Richard Hughes, a former chair of the Office for Budget Responsibility, and Jim O’Neill, a cross-bench peer and former Treasury minister.

However, none have agreed to take roles in No 10. Haldane and O’Neill have been critical of Burnham’s economic approach since he entered government, particularly on increased public spending and a lack of growth-oriented policies.

Other roles will include a new adviser on Scotland, an adviser on work and welfare who will report to the new growth director, as well as another post working across immigration, security and justice, looking at cross-border crime, exploitation and illegal migration.

articles.title: Ukraine, Russia trade strikes after Witkoff talks
articles.summary: Soon after Putin and Zelenskyy expressed willingness to resume US-mediated talks, Russia and Ukraine traded major attacks on each other's capitals.

image.caption: Kyiv's ability to defend against Russian drones and missiles has been reportedly limited after Elon Musk's Starlink restricted its speed for Ukraine's militaryImage: Evgeniy Maloletka/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russia and Ukraine traded major attacks overnight, authorities from both countries said on Thursday, shortly after US envoy Steve Witkoff held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg.
Missiles struck Kyiv in the early hours of Thursday, wounding at least 15 people, eight of whom have been hospitalized, city authorities said.
The subway infrastructure on the Southern Bridge over the Dnipro river in Kyiv was also damaged, Mayor ⁠Vitali ​Klitschko ​said ​on Telegram.

blocks.caption: Ukraine's airforce warned of Russian missiles and instructed residents to take shelterImage: Evgeniy Maloletka/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Another Russian strike killed a woman and injured four others in the Kharkiv region in northeast Ukraine, regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said on Telegram. A drone also hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure in the Poltava region, local authorities said without providing more details.
Meanwhile, Moscow's mayor said that 630 drones were launched towards the region overnight, wounding at least two people.
"Most of them were destroyed by air defense systems," Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on social media. Of these, 163 drones had been approaching the capital city, he added.
In western Russia's Lipetsk city, a man was injured as drones hit apartment buildings and a medical facility, Governor Igor Artamonov said on Telegram.
Strikes after US attempts mediation

The latest round of strikes came after US special envoy Witkoff held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway earlier this week, followed by talks with Putin in Russia on Wednesday.
The Trump administration has attempted to mediate between the two sides to end the conflict that began with Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
US aims for new round of Russia-Ukraine negotiations

Putin agreed "in principle" to resume US-mediated peace talks with Kyiv as soon as next month. Zelenskyy, too, said on Wednesday that Ukraine supported a US proposal for trilateral talks at the negotiators level to be held as soon as possible.

It was "the closest we've been" to ending the war, US President Donald Trump claimed after Witkoff's meeting with Putin. However, that did not stop the neighboring nations from keeping up a barrage of attacks.
